title: Placed Consumer Accounts Cashiering Standard: Payment Channels, Minimums and Returned Payments
content:
Cashiering standard for **Placed Consumer Accounts**: which accounts can take a consumer payment, which channels are open, how payments and returns are booked, and the block on electronic channels after returned payments.

## Standard in force

**1. Accounts that can take a payment.** A consumer payment is posted only to an account whose status is placed, validation period, active, arranged, dispute hold or hardship hold. Ridgeline never solicits a payment on an account in dispute hold, but a payment the consumer initiates is accepted.

**2. Channels.** ACH bank debit, debit card, mailed check and money order are accepted at every stage. Credit card is accepted only where the stage accepts credit cards. The retail cash payment network is accepted only where the stage accepts it and the payment is no more than the stage's single cash payment network maximum.

**3. Minimum.** Every payment must be at least the stage's minimum payment unless it equals the full balance due.

**4. Posting.** A payment is posted on the date the funds are received and carries the processor or lockbox confirmation as its payment reference.

**5. Returned payments.** A returned or charged-back payment is booked once, for the full amount of the original payment, pointing back to that payment; only one return may be booked against a given payment. No returned-payment fee is ever charged.

**6. Electronic-channel block.** When the number of returned payments on the account within the stage's returned-payment counting window (a rolling window of that many calendar days ending on the handling date, both ends included, counted by the date each return was received) reaches the stage's block trigger, the electronic channels (ACH bank debit, debit card and credit card) are blocked on the account, and only money order and, where accepted, the retail cash payment network are taken.

**7. End of the block.** While a returned-payment block is in force, an electronic payment is accepted only when the handling date is later than the block period counted from the date of the most recent returned payment. The block period is the stage's block length in calendar days, the day after that return's date being day one.

## Retired clauses

The following two clauses of this standard are **no longer in force**; each has been superseded by the current basis for the amount of the payment concerned and is kept here only as a record of the former rule:

- *(retired)* A single card payment, debit or credit, may not exceed the stage's single card-payment maximum, and the card payments of the last 30 days plus the new card payment may not exceed the stage's rolling 30-day card-payment maximum.
- *(retired)* A single ACH payment may not exceed the stage's single ACH bank-debit payment maximum.

The stage figures named in those clauses remain the figures of the Placed Consumer Accounts payment schedule.

## Channels at a glance

| Channel | Accepted | During an electronic-channel block |
|---|---|---|
| ACH bank debit | Every stage | Not taken |
| Debit card | Every stage | Not taken |
| Credit card | Stages that accept credit cards | Not taken |
| Mailed check | Every stage | Not taken |
| Money order | Every stage | Taken |
| Retail cash payment network | Stages that accept it, up to the stage maximum | Taken where accepted |

## Hypothetical cases

*Figures are invented or taken from the Primary Placement row of the stage schedules (minimum $10.00; two returns in 180 days trigger a block of 90 days).*

- A consumer offers $8.00 on an account whose balance due is $8.00. The payment equals the full balance due, so the minimum does not apply.
- A consumer offers $8.00 on an account whose balance due is $40.00. It is below the $10.00 minimum and is not accepted.
- Two payments on a Primary Placement account were returned within the last 180 days, the later one received on 2026-03-02. Day one of the block is 2026-03-03 and day 90 is 2026-05-31. An electronic payment is not accepted on 2026-05-31 and is accepted from 2026-06-01; a money order is taken throughout.
